prerequisites: Mathematical and informational knowledge required in the first year of the course, with particular reference to Euclidean, Cartesian, Algebraic and Differential Geometry.

learning_outcomes.text: The course contributes to the training of engineers able to use techniques and tools for the assisted design of components, systems and processes. It is oriented towards integrated virtual design by proposing contents relating to the main methods of computer-assisted three-dimensional graphic and geometric modeling, to the design procedures and generation of the relative documentation and to integration with the skills of dimensioning and/or choosing mechanical components. Knowledge is also provided on the main design aid tools within the product development cycle and on reverse engineering, rapid prototyping and CAXX modeling technologies.

At the end of the course, the student will be able to understand the terminology used in the field of 3D modeling; know the main 3D model management systems and the analysis and design methodologies of a virtual design system. Use the main 3D modeling tools and apply the best procedures for using virtual models with simulation software. Use commercial and standard components and parts and assemblies made by other members of the design team.
Choose the right commercial tools based on the required needs and identify the most appropriate methods to use them, possibly customizing them to optimize the design process.
Work in groups and produce and present project documentation using technical terminology correctly.

Apply the acquired knowledge also using different software, even in different fields, and extend them to the topics proposed in the Master's Degree courses in relation to surface modeling and the use of other virtual analysis tools.

syllabus_topics: Computer Graphics and CAD systems
Principal methods of representation of the geometric model
Principal modeling methods of the geometric model
Transformation matrices for computer graphics
Parametric / variational modeling
The math of the interpolating and approximating curves, the parametric curves
The mathematics of the interpolating and approximating surfaces, the parametric surfaces
Reverse engineering and physical prototyping techniques in industrial design
Modern aided design techniques in the development plan of an industrial product: virtual engineering and DMU
The use of commercial components in design
3D model files format
Project documentation
Examples of industrial cases
Use of sketches for the generation of volumes
Adding and removing volumes with linear and revolved extrusions, sweeps and lofts
Use of features (holes, ribs, emptying of slots, welding, etc.)
The creation of assemblies, the use of 3D models from the catalog and the structuring of the project
Setting the table
Checks on the model (analysis of movement, interference, disassembly and assembly, etc.)
Parameterizations, equations and configurations
teaching_methods: Teaching seminars in collaboration with industry experts

assessment_methods.method: Practical modeling test of a simple mechanism and creation of tables in accordance with the law
(Optional) Discussion of a design paper / Project work

assessment_rules: Assessment is through a theory test (30% weight, passed with 50% correct answers) and a practical modeling test (40% weight, sufficient if a simple mechanism is correctly implemented). The (optional) discussion of a design paper or a project work accounts for 40% of the evaluation and allows for achieving the maximum evaluation. The project work must include a technical report, sizing calculations, a complete 3D model, and drawings of non-commercial components.
